title.zh: ECDH 椭圆曲线密钥协商

entries.relatedPolicy: Related entries are distinct concepts; no merge or replacement is implied.

zh.principle: **算法**：ECDH 椭圆曲线密钥协商（Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman）。对于素数域曲线 secp256r1、secp384r1、secp521r1，ECDH 的密钥协商步骤印在 rfc8446.txt:5329-5334：该计算按 IEEE 1363 以 ECKAS-DH1 方案进行，得到的值用原文说就是 「the shared secret is the x-coordinate」（共享秘密是椭圆曲线 ECDH 点的 x 坐标），并以定长八位组串表示、前导零不得截断。整句因换行带缩进而被拆到多个续行，所以只引用 x 坐标这一段、其余按行号转述。关于范围有两点：这是经典的 ECDH 原语（用私有标量乘对端公钥点、取其 x 坐标），而 RFC 8446 把这个 x 坐标当作中间值而非最终密钥——密钥派生是另一条目，故此处不作断言。
zh.why: RFC 7919 讨论的是有限域 Diffie-Hellman，而正是这一框架说明了为何更倾向椭圆曲线形式：与有限域 DHE（FFDHE）相比，rfc7919.txt:720 对 ECDHE 印着 「a much stronger key exchange mechanism than FFDHE」（比 FFDHE 强得多的密钥交换机制）（在可比的计算代价下）。同一节明确说 RFC 7919 自身不涵盖仅有限域的情形、也不处理 ECDHE（文中称 ECDHE 定义于 RFC 4492）——这句话是在作比较，而不是给 ECDH 下定义。于是标准给出的设计理由是效率：椭圆曲线群能以更低的每安全级代价完成同一种协商。这正是被引文件断言的取舍；它没有声称两种设定之间存在等价性证明。
zh.used: NIST SP 800-186 把 ECDH 归入椭圆曲线的用途。整句类别陈述印在 sp800-186.txt:335-337：「Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) has uses in applications involving digital signatures (e.g., Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm [ECDSA]) and key agreement schemes (e.g., Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman [ECDH]).」（椭圆曲线密码用于数字签名（如 ECDSA）与密钥协商方案（如椭圆曲线 Diffie-Hellman 即 ECDH））。该建议还在 sp800-186.txt:357-359 附近说明其规定的密钥对仅用于签名或密钥协商、不应作其他用途。这就是证据支持的部署角色：ECDH 是这套基于离散对数的椭圆曲线家族里的密钥协商成员。同一文档正文左对齐，所以这句以普通单空格接合、可整段引用。
zh.broken: ECDH 的难度只等同于它背后的椭圆曲线离散对数问题，而 SP 800-186 记录了让这一假设站得住的归约。在 sp800-186.txt:2184-2198 的曲线选择准则里，第 5 条印着椭圆曲线离散对数问题可被转化为 「an ordinary discrete logarithm problem defined over the finite field GF(qk)」（定义在有限域 GF(qk) 上的普通离散对数问题）（即 MOV 型迁移）；GF(q^k) 的上标与随后的同余号在本抽取中退化，所以嵌入度的条件按行号转述而不引用。正因为这一归约存在，同一准则要求每条曲线都有大嵌入度、小余因子的大素数阶子群、以及非异常曲线的阶。这里没有说的：本留存文件不提量子计算机，所以该条目不把量子破解附加到 ECDH 上——经典边界就是该归约，而标准划出的防线是能抵抗它的曲线选择。
zh.history: 留存文本记录的是 ECDH 何时进入标准，而非谁发明了它。RFC 7568（2015 年 6 月，运行页眉在 rfc7568.txt:60）在列举较新 TLS 版本相对 SSLv3 新增的特性时，于 rfc7568.txt:205 印着 「Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH)」（椭圆曲线 Diffie-Hellman（ECDH）），紧接着说明 ECDH 与 ECDSA 是在 RFC 4492 中加入——续行带缩进，故只引用 (ECDH) 这一术语、RFC 4492 的归属作转述。RFC 7919（2016 年 8 月）把 ECDHE 当作由 RFC 4492 定义的既有机制，并与自身的有限域范围作比较。这些留存文件都没有给出 ECDH 原语的提出者或首次发表年代，所以该条目只陈述文中确实印出的、可定年的标准化节点，不作无法核实的起源声明。

**形式模型与复算步骤**

\[K=g^{ab}\bmod p\quad\text{或}\quad K=[ab]G\]

ECDH 椭圆曲线密钥协商的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：a,b 私有随机数，g 生成元，p 模数，G 椭圆曲线基点。1.双方各自生成私钥并计算公钥。2.交换公钥。3.用对方公钥与自己的私钥计算共享点。边界：公式只覆盖已登记的参数与假设；参数取值、标准版本和实现细节仍以来源为准。

en.principle: **Algorithm**: Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH 椭圆曲线密钥协商). The ECDH key-agreement step, for the prime curves secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1, is printed at rfc8446.txt:5329-5334: the calculation follows IEEE 1363 under the ECKAS-DH1 scheme, and the derived value is, in the file's own words, "the shared secret is the x-coordinate" of the ECDH shared-secret elliptic curve point, expressed as a fixed-length octet string whose leading zeros are not to be truncated. The full sentence wraps across indented continuation lines, so only that x-coordinate fragment is quoted and the rest is stated by line reference. Two points about scope: this is the classical ECDH primitive (multiply the peer's public point by your private scalar, take the x-coordinate), and RFC 8446 treats the x-coordinate as an intermediate value rather than a finished key - a separate claim covers the key derivation, so it is not asserted here.
en.why: RFC 7919 is about finite-field Diffie-Hellman, and it is that framing that states the reason to prefer the elliptic-curve form: measured against finite-field DHE (FFDHE), the retained text prints, at rfc7919.txt:720, "a much stronger key exchange mechanism than FFDHE" for ECDHE at comparable computational cost. The same section is explicit that RFC 7919 itself does not cover finite-field-only cases nor address ECDHE (which it says is defined in RFC 4492) - the point of the sentence is comparative, not a definition of ECDH. So the design reason the standards give is efficiency: an elliptic-curve group delivers the same style of agreement at lower cost per security level than the finite-field construction. This is exactly the trade the cited document asserts; it does not claim a proof of equivalence between the two settings.
en.used: NIST SP 800-186 places ECDH among the uses of elliptic curves. The whole category sentence is printed at sp800-186.txt:335-337: "Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) has uses in applications involving digital signatures (e.g., Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm [ECDSA]) and key agreement schemes (e.g., Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman [ECDH])." The Recommendation also states, near sp800-186.txt:357-359, that the key pairs it specifies are for signature or key agreement only and should not be used for other purposes. That is the deployment role the evidence supports: ECDH is the key-agreement member of the discrete-log-based elliptic-curve family. The same document is left-aligned, so this sentence rejoins with ordinary single spaces and is quoted intact.
en.broken: ECDH is only as hard as the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem behind it, and SP 800-186 records the reduction that keeps that assumption honest. In the curve-selection criteria at sp800-186.txt:2184-2198, item 5 prints that "an ordinary discrete logarithm problem defined over the finite field GF(qk)" is what the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem can be converted into (this is the MOV-type transfer); the superscript in GF(q^k) and the congruence sign that follows degrade in this extraction, so the embedding-degree condition is stated by line rather than quoted. Because that reduction exists, the same criteria require each curve to have a large embedding degree, a prime-order subgroup with small cofactor, and a non-anomalous order, so the transfer to the finite-field setting stays infeasible. What is not said here: this retained document does not mention quantum computers, so no quantum-break claim is attached to ECDH in this entry - the classical limit is the reduction, and the boundary the standards draw is curve selection that resists it.
en.history: The retained texts date when ECDH entered a standard, not who invented it. RFC 7568 (June 2015, running header at rfc7568.txt:60) lists, among the features that recent TLS versions added over SSLv3, "Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH)" at rfc7568.txt:205, and the very next words say that ECDH and ECDSA are added in RFC 4492 - the continuation wraps with indentation, so only the (ECDH) term is quoted and the RFC 4492 attribution is paraphrased. RFC 7919 (August 2016) treats ECDHE as an established mechanism defined by RFC 4492 and compares it against its own finite-field scope. None of these retained documents gives an author or a first-publication date for the ECDH primitive itself, so this entry states only the dated standardization the sources actually print and no origin it cannot verify.

zh: ECDH（椭圆曲线 Diffie-Hellman）：基于椭圆曲线群离散对数的密钥协商方案（sp800-186:335-337）。
共享秘密 x 坐标：ECDH 算出的值，即 ECDH 共享秘密椭圆曲线点的 x 坐标（rfc8446:5333）。
ECKAS-DH1：rfc8446:5329-5334 中素数域曲线 ECDH 计算所依据的 IEEE 1363 方案。
ECDHE：带临时（ephemeral）密钥的 ECDH 密钥交换，rfc7919 称其定义于 RFC 4492。
FFDHE：有限域临时 Diffie-Hellman；rfc7919 与 ECDHE 在计算代价上作比较。
嵌入度归约：ECDLP 可被转成有限域 DLP（MOV 型），故标准要求大嵌入度（sp800-186:2184-2198）。
en: ECDH: elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman, a key-agreement scheme over an elliptic-curve group (sp800-186:335-337).
x-coordinate shared secret: the ECDH value, the x-coordinate of the shared elliptic-curve point (rfc8446:5333).
ECKAS-DH1: the IEEE 1363 scheme the prime-curve ECDH calculation follows (rfc8446:5329-5334).
ECDHE: the ephemeral-key ECDH key exchange; rfc7919 says it is defined in RFC 4492.
FFDHE: finite-field Diffie-Hellman ephemeral, compared with ECDHE for cost in rfc7919.
embedding-degree reduction: ECDLP convertible to finite-field DLP (MOV-type), hence the large-embedding-degree requirement (sp800-186:2184-2198).
